note: Ramond et al. (2023) confirmed feeding difficulties and infantile spasms are core features of Ramond-Elliott syndrome, but infantile spasms are widely shared across diverse microcephalic DEEs, making this combination unspecific among epileptic encephalopathies.

evidence.text: Affected individuals with TRA2B variants presented intellectual disability or developmental delay frequently associated with infantile spasms, microcephaly, brain anomalies, and feeding difficulties.

source.title: Clustered variants in the 5′ coding region of TRA2B cause a distinctive neurodevelopmental syndrome
source.quote: All affected individuals presented intellectual disability and/or developmental delay, frequently associated with infantile spasms, microcephaly, brain anomalies, autism spectrum disorder, feeding difficulties, and short stature.

evidence.text: Infantile spasms represent an early-onset epileptic encephalopathy where diverse structural and genetic etiologies (such as STXBP1 and other DEE genes) converge on a shared electroclinical pattern.

source.title: Infantile Spasms (West Syndrome): Integrating Genetic ... - PMC
source.quote: Infantile spasms (ISs), or West syndrome (WS), represent an early-onset epileptic encephalopathy in which diverse structural, genetic, metabolic, infectious, and neurocutaneous conditions converge on a shared pattern of hypsarrhythmia, clustered spasms, and later developmental impairment.
